canonical_name: PicoRV32 -- a size-optimised RISC-V CPU core in Verilog (Clifford Wolf / YosysHQ)
lineage: PicoRV32 (2015-, Clifford Wolf): a small RV32I[MC] processor as synthesisable Verilog with a self-checking testbench; the reference small core of the open RISC-V / Yosys ecosystem
version: github.com/YosysHQ/picorv32 main branch as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes)
dependencies: a RISC-V gcc for the firmware test (optional)

example.command: iverilog -o tb testbench.v picorv32.v && vvp tb
example.input: a compiled firmware image or the built-in test
example.output: the testbench's PASS/trap report and register trace

human_capability_summary.built_to: execute the RISC-V RV32I instruction set as a small synthesisable processor -- fetch, decode, a state-machine control path, register file, and an ALU -- for FPGAs and teaching
human_capability_summary.pressure: silicon area and timing: the core trades cycles-per-instruction for a tiny gate count, an explicit area/speed decision
human_capability_summary.success_means: correct execution of RISC-V programs (its self-checking testbench passes) within the gate budget

known_human_problem_solved: running a real instruction set on minimal hardware

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run picorv32
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: execute the RISC-V RV32I instruction set as a small synthesisable processor -- fetch, decode, a state-machine control path, register file, and an ALU -- for FPGAs and teaching
